findings.text: root_path is interpolated into the regex without re.escape(). A root_path containing metacharacters, such as '/api(v1' or '/a+b', raises re.error or matches the wrong text. For example, root_path='/a.b' also strips '/axb/items', so the route path comes out wrong.

The prefix is stripped with no path-segment boundary check. With root_path='/app' and path='/application/x', the result is 'lication/x', which has no leading slash and routes wrongly. The right behavior is to strip only when path == root_path or path starts with root_path + '/'.
